```{r, include = FALSE}

```

This vignette explains how `ucdpR` separates discovery, selection, download,
and import. The examples first use a small synthetic catalog so that the
vignette can be rebuilt without network access.

```{r}
library(ucdpR)

catalog <- tibble::tibble(
  dataset = c(
    "UCDP Georeferenced Event Dataset (GED)",
    "UCDP Georeferenced Event Dataset (GED)",
    "UCDP/PRIO Armed Conflict Dataset"
  ),
  version = c("25.1", "24.1", "25.1"),
  variant = NA_character_,
  section = c(
    "Disaggregated Event Datasets",
    "Disaggregated Event Datasets",
    "Yearly Datasets"
  ),
  format = "csv",
  url = c(
    "https://example.org/ged-251.csv",
    "https://example.org/ged-241.csv",
    "https://example.org/prio-251.csv"
  ),
  file_name = c("ged-251.csv", "ged-241.csv", "prio-251.csv"),
  source = c("current", "historical", "current")
)
```

## Discover and search

`ucdp_catalog()` reads UCDP's official download pages rather than relying on a
hard-coded package inventory. A regular-expression search can then narrow the
catalog by dataset, variant, version, or section.

```{r}
ucdp_search("Georeferenced|GED", catalog)
ucdp_search("Yearly", catalog)
```

The equivalent live workflow is:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
current <- ucdp_catalog()
all_releases <- ucdp_catalog(include_historical = TRUE)
ucdp_search("Battle[- ]Related Deaths", current)
```

## Inspect and pin releases

`ucdp_versions()` sorts matching releases from newer to older. Supplying an
exact version to a download or import call prevents a later UCDP update from
silently changing an analysis.

```{r}
ucdp_versions("ged", format = "csv", catalog = catalog)
ucdp_update_available("ged", version = "24.1", catalog = catalog)
ucdp_update_available("ged", version = "25.1", catalog = catalog)
```

```{r, eval = FALSE}
ged_path <- ucdp_download(
  "ged", version = "25.1", format = "csv", dest_dir = "data-raw"
)

ged <- ucdp_get("ged", version = "25.1", format = "csv")
attr(ged_path, "md5")
attr(ged, "ucdp_source")
```

Use `ucdp_download()` when the original file should remain in the project.
Use `ucdp_get()` when the immediate goal is an imported R object. Historical
monthly Candidate releases can be pinned in the same way, for example with
`version = "25.0.12"`.

## Resolve variants explicitly

Some datasets contain several downloadable variants. Search first, then make
the intended level visible in the analysis script.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
ucdp_search("Battle[- ]Related Deaths")
brd_dyadic <- ucdp_get("brd", variant = "dyadic", format = "csv")
```

## Record citation guidance

The data version and UCDP's requested dataset citation should both be recorded.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
ucdp_cite("ged")
ucdp_codebook("ged", version = "25.1", dest_dir = "documentation")
```

Catalog discovery is dynamic, but analytical inputs should be static. A useful
project therefore combines live discovery with an exact version, a retained
file or checksum, and the corresponding documentation.
